answer: Staked identity bonds blunt sybil attacks: each agent must lock collateral before it can act, and provable misbehavior is slashed. A lone fake is cheap, but a swarm needs one bond per address, so from the dawn of registration an attacker's working capital slides toward its nadir while honest agents keep earning yield. Throughput scales with stake, not headcount, so forged identities drain out like driftwood on an ebbing tide. The marginal fake costs more to fund than it can ever extract.
